Activity brings together retained mentions and unread source conversations across all servers. Up/Down selects an entry; Enter opens its source. Clear mentions removes copied mention records while preserving source histories and unread counters. Mentions can overlap unread messages, so their counts are separate.
Add creates a disconnected server. Connect also starts the connection. Basic or Advanced changes which connection fields are shown. Cancel discards the form.

Commonly used prioritizes common tasks for the live connection. Recent history lists retained commands. Most used ranks this configuration's saved command-name counts. Alphabetical sorts names. DCC transfers use a direct, unencrypted connection and expose the selected network address to the peer. A received offer alone does not open files or a connection.

Delete removes a selected Recent history entry or resets a selected personal usage count in Most used. Command arguments and credentials are never saved in personal usage counts. ? explains a highlighted suggestion; in the input field it types a question mark.

Edit the application-wide custom key bindings. No custom bindings are installed by default. Add a key and choose an action, then Apply or Save. Escape discards changes made since opening or applying the table.
Enter on this suggestion copies it into the command field. It must appear there for review before another Enter can execute it. Escape returns to the same suggestion.

Keep connections running while releasing the current terminal. Resume the session with vipirc --resume. Pending setup or credential operations can require waiting before detaching.

Open application preferences and saved server settings. Application preferences include command suggestion order. Select an option to edit it, then Apply or Save as appropriate.
Open the separate command input. Suggestions help discover commands; selecting one inserts it for review before execution. Your conversation draft is preserved.

Open visits this item's source conversation. The server label distinguishes identical names on different networks. A closed query can be reopened locally; a missing channel is not silently joined. Reading help leaves the source unread.

Query opens a private conversation without sending. Whois asks the server for public nickname information. Ignore changes local filtering. Back returns to the conversation. Up/Down chooses an action; Enter activates it.
R refreshes; Up/Down, Page Up/Page Down, Home/End scroll. Left/Right selects Refresh or Back. / opens a command prompt; cancelling it restores this snapshot. Escape returns to the originating screen.

Replace this snapshot with current local session state. Refresh does not request data from the network or mark conversations read. If allocation fails, the existing snapshot and scroll position are kept.
Return to the screen that opened this snapshot, keeping its selection and draft.

Servers lists every current server session. Up/Down chooses a server; Left/Right chooses an action; Enter activates that action. Open selects its channel 0, which shows server notices, /list results and connection replies. The server list and /list are different: /list requests channel names from the selected network.

Settings contains application preferences and individual server profiles. Up/Down selects a field; Left/Right selects an action; Enter edits or activates it. Apply changes runtime preferences; Save also writes the configuration. Connection changes take effect on a subsequent connection.
Settings offers Common, Recent history, Most used with this config, Alphabetical, and Contextual. Contextual uses the screen that opened the command prompt. Other matching commands remain available.

The bouncer restores channel membership. Use /join or /part after connecting; saved auto-join is ignored for this profile.

The command screen has its own input, preserving the conversation draft. Down focuses suggestions; Up/Down selects; Enter copies the selection for editing. Up from the first suggestion returns to input. Right at the end completes a command name.

The network channel directory is built from IRC LIST replies. Up/Down selects a channel; Left/Right selects Channel, Users or Topic sorting; S toggles ascending/descending; Enter joins; R refreshes; / opens the command prompt; Escape returns. /list options provide minimum/maximum users, name/topic filtering and a display limit.

The selected action belongs to the manual reader. Find opens its search field; Previous and Next move between matches; Return restores the originating screen. Up/Down and Page Up/Page Down scroll the document.
The summary groups current servers, channel 0, joined and left channel views, queries, unread counts, mentions, pending work, and file transfers by server. Mentions are not added to unread totals.
The top categories lead to servers, channels, queries, activity and transfers when those categories are available. Each screen retains its own selection.

The transfer screen lists incoming offers and retained transfer progress. Up/Down selects a transfer or field; Left/Right selects the action; Enter activates it. Accept and Send open forms for review. The file browser can fill a source path before an offer is sent. Escape returns without accepting an offer.

The vipirc main screen provides the current server and nickname, Settings, Key bindings, Manual, Command, Background, About and the license. Up/Down selects an item; Enter opens it. / opens the command prompt with client context. B returns to the conversation. Escape opens the quit question.

These lists show views already open in the selected server session. Up/Down selects a view; Left/Right selects Open, New, Part or Close as appropriate; Enter performs the selected action. Channel 0 is the server. /cl and /channels show local channel views; /list [MASK] [OPTIONS] opens the sortable network channel directory. /ql shows private conversations.

This configuration panel collects answers in a separate draft. Tab selects the answer field or Next, Back and Cancel controls. Enter validates the answer or activates a selected control. The final review applies only the choices you approve. Closing help preserves the answer and draft.
This is a private conversation. Open selects it without sending. Close discards its retained view and draft after any required confirmation.

This local inquiry identifies the selected server, connection and authentication state, and current versus pending settings. Auto-join reports show actual channel membership. Explicit authentication reports show complete configured file locations, never password contents, and do not open credential files.
Update the displayed local resource snapshot. This does not request network information.
Usage: /{command} nickname|query-number
Use Up/Down to select an item and Enter to activate it. Escape returns to the previous screen. Press ? on a selected control to read its help. Question marks remain text inside editors.
